analyst_view.overall: Crystal Palace (21st) and Real Sociedad (20th) both have 5 points and sit just outside the play-off places, so both need a result. Palace sacked Pierre Sage and lost Thomas Frank's first game 3-2 at Coventry, their fifth league defeat in a row, and they have conceded at least twice in 11 of 17 games this season; the numbers know nothing about the manager change. Adam Wharton is banned in Europe, Ismaila Sarr, Chadi Riad and Takehiro Tomiyasu are out, Oscar Mingueza is doubtful and Cheick Doucoure is not registered, while Yeremy Pino and Jean-Philippe Mateta serve Premier League bans only and can play (Sports Mole, The Hard Tackle). Correction to this morning's view: Real Sociedad's squad list leaves out Jon Aramburu after his hip knock at Racing, as the numbers already assumed, with Hector Fort likely at right-back; Barrenetxea, Odriozola and Yangel Herrera are also out and Luka Sucic is fit. Norwegian referee Rohit Saggi (about 3.8 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and already add 6.2% to Palace's side for Aramburu's absence, which the squad list confirms, so this morning's reason for a cut is gone. Palace lose Wharton, their main passer, which the numbers do not know, but they also concede a lot (two or more in 11 of 17 games) and Mateta and Pino are available, so the two pull opposite ways and I stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, already nudged up for Real Sociedad's 40 corners in their last six. Palace keep Pino and McNeil wide and Sociedad have Kubo, Guedes and the attacking left-back Sergio Gomez, so nothing points either way and I stay at 9.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already lifted for Palace's 15 bookings in six games and trimmed for referee Rohit Saggi's calm record (3.8 a game). Wharton, who often picks up cards, is out, but two sides level on points under a new Palace manager make for a tense game, so the two balance and I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, with Real Sociedad's busy recent shooting (106 in six) already adding about 19% to their side. Palace's midfield without Wharton (Timber, Hughes and Kamada expected) should build less, which the numbers do not see, so I shade it slightly, to about 26.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target, already a little lower for Palace's quieter recent attack. Palace's forwards Mateta, Strand Larsen and Pino are available and Sociedad have Oyarzabal, Kubo and a fit Sucic, so the finishers are mostly there and I stay at 9.4.
